Of 169 kittens, 127 died before they were six months old due to a trauma caused in most cases by dog attacks and road accidents.<sup about="#mwt668" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Nutter2004_175-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Nutter2004"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Nutter2004-175"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Nutter2004-175" id="mwBZ4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBZ8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBaA">[</span>174<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBaE">]</span></span></a></sup> The first litter is usually smaller than subsequent litters. Kittens are weaned between six and seven weeks of age. Queens normally reach sexual maturity at 5–10 months, and males at 5–7 months. This varies depending on breed.<sup about="#mwt669" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-compendium_171-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"compendium"}}"><a href="#cite_note-compendium-171" id="mwBaI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBaM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBaQ">[</span>170<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBaU">]</span></span></a></sup> Kittens reach <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puberty" title="Puberty" id="mwBaY">puberty</a> at the age of 9–10 months.<sup about="#mwt670" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Jemmett1977_168-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Jemmett1977"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Jemmett1977-168" id="mwBac"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBag"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBak">[</span>167<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBao">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBas">Cats are ready to go to new homes at about 12 weeks of age, when they are ready to leave their mother.<sup about="#mwt673" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-176" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-176"}}"><a href="#cite_note-176" id="mwBaw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBa0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBa4">[</span>175<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBa8">]</span></span></a></sup> They can be surgically <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutering" title="Neutering" id="mwBbA">sterilized</a> (spayed or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castration" title="Castration" id="mwBbE">castrated</a>) as early as seven weeks to limit unwanted reproduction.<sup about="#mwt676" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-177" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-177"}}"><a href="#cite_note-177" id="mwBbI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBbM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbQ">[</span>176<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbU">]</span></span></a></sup> This surgery also prevents undesirable sex-related behavior, such as aggression, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spraying_(animal_behavior)" title="Spraying (animal behavior)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBbY">territory marking</a> (spraying urine) in males, and yowling (calling) in females. Traditionally, this surgery was performed at around six to nine months of age, but it is increasingly being performed before <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puberty" title="Puberty" id="mwBbc">puberty</a>, at about three to six months.<sup about="#mwt679" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-178" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-178"}}"><a href="#cite_note-178" id="mwBbg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBbk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbo">[</span>177<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbs">]</span></span></a></sup> In the United States, about 80% of household cats are neutered.<sup about="#mwt682" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-179" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-179"}}"><a href="#cite_note-179" id="mwBbw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBb0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBb4">[</span>178<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBb8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="29" id="mwBcA" aria-labelledby="Lifespan_and_health"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Lifespan_and_health">Lifespan and health</h2></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt683" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBcE" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Main","href":"./Template:Main"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Cat health"},"2":{"wt":"Aging in cats"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441" about="#mwt684" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt683" id="mwBcI">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_health" title="Cat health">Cat health</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aging_in_cats" title="Aging in cats">Aging in cats</a></div>

<p id="mwBcM">The average lifespan of pet cats has risen in recent decades. In the early 1980s, it was about 7 years,<sup about="#mwt689" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Kraft1998_180-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Kraft1998"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Kraft1998-180"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Kraft1998-180" id="mwBcQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBcU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBcY">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBcc">]</span></span></a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap" about="#mwt685" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBcg" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"rp","href":"./Template:Rp"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"33"}},"i":0}}]}"><span title="Page / location: 33"><span typeof="mw:Entity">:</span><span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>33<span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span></span></sup><sup about="#mwt692" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Nassar_1984_181-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Nassar 1984"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Nassar_1984-181"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Nassar_1984-181" id="mwBck"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBco"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBcs">[</span>180<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBcw">]</span></span></a></sup> rising to 9.4 years in 1995<sup about="#mwt693" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Kraft1998_180-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Kraft1998"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Kraft1998-180" id="mwBc0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBc4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBc8">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBdA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap" about="#mwt686" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBdE" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"rp","href":"./Template:Rp"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"33"}},"i":0}}]}"><span title="Page / location: 33"><span typeof="mw:Entity">:</span><span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>33<span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span></span></sup> and an average of about 13 years as of 2014 and 2023.<sup about="#mwt696" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-182" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-182"}}"><a href="#cite_note-182" id="mwBdI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBdM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBdQ">[</span>181<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBdU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt699" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-183" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-183"}}"><a href="#cite_note-183" id="mwBdY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBdc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBdg">[</span>182<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBdk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBdo">Neutering increases life expectancy; one 2024 study found neutered cats to live one year longer than entire cats.<sup about="#mwt702" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-184" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-184"}}"><a href="#cite_note-184" id="mwBds"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBdw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBd0">[</span>183<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBd4">]</span></span></a></sup> Having a cat <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutering" title="Neutering" id="mwBd8">neutered</a> confers some health benefits, such as a decreased incidence of reproductive <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasia" title="Neoplasia" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBeA">neoplasia</a>.<sup about="#mwt705" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Obesity1_185-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Obesity1"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Obesity1-185"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Obesity1-185" id="mwBeE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBeI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBeM">[</span>184<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBeQ">]</span></span></a></sup> However, neutering decreases metabolism<sup about="#mwt708" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-186" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-186"}}"><a href="#cite_note-186" id="mwBeU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBeY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBec">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBeg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt711" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Obesity2_187-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Obesity2"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Obesity2-187"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Obesity2-187" id="mwBek"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBeo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBes">[</span>186<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBew">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt714" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Obesity3_188-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Obesity3"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Obesity3-188"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Obesity3-188" id="mwBe0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBe4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBe8">[</span>187<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfA">]</span></span></a></sup> and increases food intake,<sup about="#mwt715" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Obesity3_188-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Obesity3"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Obesity3-188" id="mwBfE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBfI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfM">[</span>187<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt718" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Obesity4_189-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Obesity4"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Obesity4-189"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Obesity4-189" id="mwBfU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBfY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfc">[</span>188<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfg">]</span></span></a></sup> both of which can cause obesity in neutered cats.<sup about="#mwt721" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Obesity5_190-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Obesity5"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Obesity5-190"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Obesity5-190" id="mwBfk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBfo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfs">[</span>189<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfw">]</span></span></a></sup> Pre-pubertal neutering (neutering at 4 months or earlier) was only recommended by 28% of American veterinarians in one study. Some concerns of early neutering were metabolic, retarded <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epiphyseal_plate" title="Epiphyseal plate" id="mwBf0">physeal closure</a>, and urinary tract disease related.<sup about="#mwt724" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-191" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-191"}}"><a href="#cite_note-191" id="mwBf4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBf8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBgA">[</span>190<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBgE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="30" id="mwBgI" aria-labelledby="Disease"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Disease">Disease</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt725" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBgM" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Main","href":"./Template:Main"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"List of feline diseases"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441" about="#mwt726" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt725" id="mwBgQ">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_feline_diseases" title="List of feline diseases">List of feline diseases</a></div>

<p id="mwBgU">About 250 heritable <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder" title="Genetic disorder" id="mwBgY">genetic disorders</a> have been identified in cats; many are similar to human <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inborn_errors_of_metabolism" title="Inborn errors of metabolism" id="mwBgc">inborn errors of metabolism</a>.<sup about="#mwt729" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-192" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-192"}}"><a href="#cite_note-192" id="mwBgg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBgk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBgo">[</span>191<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBgs">]</span></span></a></sup> The high level of similarity among the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolism" title="Metabolism" id="mwBgw">metabolism</a> of mammals allows many of these feline diseases to be diagnosed using <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_testing" title="Genetic testing" id="mwBg0">genetic tests</a> that were originally developed for use in humans, as well as the use of cats as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_model" title="Animal model" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBg4">animal models</a> in the study of the human diseases.<sup about="#mwt732" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-193" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-193"}}"><a href="#cite_note-193" id="mwBg8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBhA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhE">[</span>192<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhI">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt735" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-194" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-194"}}"><a href="#cite_note-194" id="mwBhM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBhQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhU">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhY">]</span></span></a></sup> Diseases affecting domestic cats include acute infections, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitic_disease" title="Parasitic disease" id="mwBhc">parasitic infestations</a>, injuries, and chronic diseases such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chronic_kidney_disease_in_cats" title="Chronic kidney disease in cats" id="mwBhg">kidney disease</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feline_hyperthyroidism" title="Feline hyperthyroidism" id="mwBhk">hyperthyroidism</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthritis" title="Arthritis" id="mwBho">arthritis</a>. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feline_vaccination" title="Feline vaccination" id="mwBhs">Vaccinations</a> are available for many infectious diseases, as are treatments to eliminate parasites such as worms, ticks, and fleas.<sup about="#mwt738" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-195" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-195"}}"><a href="#cite_note-195" id="mwBhw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBh0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBh4">[</span>194<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBh8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="31" id="mwBiA" aria-labelledby="Health_issues"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Health_issues">Health issues</h2></div>
<p id="mwBiE">Between 50% and 90% of cats experience <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_pathology" title="Tooth pathology" id="mwBiI">dental</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gums" title="Gums" id="mwBiM">gum</a> problems, but these can be prevented by maintaining the cat's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_hygiene" title="Oral hygiene" id="mwBiQ">oral hygiene</a> using products specifically designed for cats, which are not toxic for them.<sup about="#mwt741" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-CollegeDental_196-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"CollegeDental"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-CollegeDental-196"}}"><a href="#cite_note-CollegeDental-196" id="mwBiU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBiY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBic">[</span>195<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBig">]</span></span></a></sup>
Accidental <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisoning" title="Poisoning" id="mwBik">poisoning</a> in cats is common and can result from several sources: plants that are toxic to cats, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medications" title="Medications" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBio">medications</a> not intended for cats, foods unsuitable for cats, and household substances such as pesticides and household cleaners.<sup about="#mwt744" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-CollegeHazards_197-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"CollegeHazards"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-CollegeHazards-197"}}"><a href="#cite_note-CollegeHazards-197" id="mwBis"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBiw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBi0">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBi4">]</span></span></a></sup> Plants toxic to cats include <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilium" title="Lilium" id="mwBi8">lilies</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulip" title="Tulip" id="mwBjA">tulips</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philodendron" title="Philodendron" id="mwBjE">philodendrons</a>; medication poisoning occurs when cats ingest drugs intended for human, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetaminophen" title="Acetaminophen" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBjI">acetaminophen</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aspirin" title="Aspirin" id="mwBjM">aspirin</a>, as well as vitamin capsules, flea treatments designed for dogs, and foods dangerous to cats like <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grapes" title="Grapes" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBjQ">grapes</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onions" title="Onions" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBjU">onions</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garlic" title="Garlic" id="mwBjY">garlic</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocolate" title="Chocolate" id="mwBjc">chocolate</a>.<sup about="#mwt745" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-CollegeHazards_197-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"CollegeHazards"}}"><a href="#cite_note-CollegeHazards-197" id="mwBjg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBjk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBjo">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBjs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBjw">Cat owners' attitudes and knowledge affects how they care for their cats, and people with greater knowledge about cats are less likely to use <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positive_punishment" title="Positive punishment" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBj0">positive punishment</a>, i.e. causing an unpleasant <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(psychology)" title="Stimulus (psychology)" id="mwBj4">stimulus</a> to the cat.<sup about="#mwt748" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Grigg2019_198-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Grigg2019"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Grigg2019-198"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Grigg2019-198" id="mwBj8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBkA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkE">[</span>197<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkI">]</span></span></a></sup>
Several organizations have published guidelines for the proper and safe care of cats. The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_for_the_Prevention_of_Cruelty_to_Animals" title="American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals" id="mwBkM">American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals</a> has published a general guide emphasizing proper cat care, which covers appropriate <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrition" title="Nutrition" id="mwBkQ">nutrition</a> and needs for fresh and clean water, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_coat" title="Animal coat" id="mwBkU">coat</a> care, litter box maintenance, regular veterinary care.<sup about="#mwt751" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ASPCAgeneral_199-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ASPCAgeneral"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-ASPCAgeneral-199"}}"><a href="#cite_note-ASPCAgeneral-199" id="mwBkY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBkc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkg">[</span>198<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkk">]</span></span></a></sup> 
The American Association of Feline Practitioners and the International Society of Feline Medicine released a guide on environmental needs of cats.<sup about="#mwt754" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Ellis2013_200-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Ellis2013"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Ellis2013-200"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Ellis2013-200" id="mwBko"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBks"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkw">[</span>199<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBk0">]</span></span></a></sup>
Professional organizations have emphasized the importance of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_enrichment" title="Environmental enrichment" id="mwBk4">environmental enrichment</a> for cats,<sup about="#mwt755" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Ellis2013_200-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Ellis2013"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Ellis2013-200" id="mwBk8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBlA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlE">[</span>199<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlI">]</span></span></a></sup> and some authors have raised concerns that many cat owners do not provide sufficient environmental enrichment. In an online survey of cat owners, only about half of the respondents reported playing with their cats daily.<sup about="#mwt756" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Grigg2019_198-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Grigg2019"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Grigg2019-198" id="mwBlM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBlQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlU">[</span>197<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBlc">Guidelines have also been published for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veterinarians" title="Veterinarians" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBlg">veterinarians</a> and caregivers to improve the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_welfare" title="Animal welfare" id="mwBlk">welfare</a> of cats under their care, including recommendations for cat-friendly interactions in veterinary clinics.<sup about="#mwt759" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Rodan2022_201-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Rodan2022"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Rodan2022-201"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Rodan2022-201" id="mwBlo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBls"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlw">[</span>200<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBl0">]</span></span></a></sup>
The guide focuses on five main aspects: providing a safe private space for the cat (e.g., a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardboard" title="Cardboard" id="mwBl4">cardboard</a> box on its side, placed in a high location, and in sufficient numbers if multiple cats are present); offering multiple environmental resources (several feeding stations, resting areas and litter boxes, and separating food from water); opportunities for play and activities that simulate <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="#Hunting_and_feeding" class="mw-selflink-fragment" id="mwBl8">hunting behavior</a> (using appropriate toys and puzzle feeders); positive, consistent, and predictable social interaction (acclimating the cat to frequent contact from an early age, speaking softly, and avoiding forced contact); and an environment that allows the cat to use its sense of smell normally (providing scratching posts and other items where it can leave its <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scent" title="Scent" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBmA">scent</a>, and avoiding strong odors throughout the home).<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_unsourced_statements" about="#mwt760" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBmE" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"cn","href":"./Template:Cn"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"June 2026"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_unsourced_statements_from_June_2026" about="#mwt760"><sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt760" id="mwBmI"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2026)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="32" id="mwBmM" aria-labelledby="Ecology"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Ecology">Ecology</h2></div>
<section data-mw-section-id="33" id="mwBmQ" aria-labelledby="Habitats"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Habitats">Habitats</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBmU"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Siamese_cat_of_Altai_shepherds.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBmY"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Siamese_cat_of_Altai_shepherds.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Siamese_cat_of_Altai_shepherds.jpg/250px-Siamese_cat_of_Altai_shepherds.jpg" decoding="async" data-file-width="4896" data-file-height="3264" data-file-type="bitmap" height="167" width="250" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Siamese_cat_of_Altai_shepherds.jpg/500px-Siamese_cat_of_Altai_shepherds.jpg 2x" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBmc"></a><figcaption id="mwBmg">A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorpoint_Shorthair" title="Colorpoint Shorthair" id="mwBmk">colourpoint domestic shorthair cat</a> living among the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yurts" title="Yurts" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBmo">yurts</a> of shepherds in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altai_Mountains" title="Altai Mountains" id="mwBms">Altai Mountains</a>, Russia</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwBmw">The domestic cat is a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmopolitan_species" title="Cosmopolitan species" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBm0">cosmopolitan species</a> and occurs across much of the world.<sup about="#mwt761" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Lipinski_52-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Lipinski"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Lipinski-52" id="mwBm4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBm8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnA">[</span>51<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnE">]</span></span></a></sup> It is adaptable and now present on all continents except <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctica" title="Antarctica" id="mwBnI">Antarctica</a>, and on 118 of the 131 main groups of islands, even on the remote <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerguelen_Islands" title="Kerguelen Islands" id="mwBnM">Kerguelen Islands</a>.<sup about="#mwt764" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-202" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-202"}}"><a href="#cite_note-202" id="mwBnQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBnU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnY">[</span>201<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnc">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt767" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-203" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-203"}}"><a href="#cite_note-203" id="mwBng"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBnk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBno">[</span>202<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBns">]</span></span></a></sup> Due to its ability to thrive in almost any terrestrial habitat, it is among the world's most <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasive_species" title="Invasive species" id="mwBnw">invasive species</a>.<sup about="#mwt770" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-204" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-204"}}"><a href="#cite_note-204" id="mwBn0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBn4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBn8">[</span>203<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoA">]</span></span></a></sup> It lives on small islands with no human inhabitants.<sup about="#mwt773" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-205" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-205"}}"><a href="#cite_note-205" id="mwBoE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBoI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoM">[</span>204<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Feral cats can live in forests, grasslands, tundra, coastal areas, agricultural land, scrublands, urban areas, and wetlands.<sup about="#mwt776" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ISSG_2006_206-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"ISSG 2006"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-ISSG_2006-206"}}"><a href="#cite_note-ISSG_2006-206" id="mwBoU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBoY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoc">[</span>205<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBog">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBok">The unwantedness that leads to the domestic cat being <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_predation_on_wildlife#Impact_by_location" title="Cat predation on wildlife" id="mwBoo">treated as an invasive species</a> is twofold. As it is little altered from the wildcat, it can readily interbreed with the wildcat. This <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_(biology)" title="Hybrid (biology)" id="mwBos">hybridization</a> poses a danger to the genetic distinctiveness of some wildcat populations, particularly in Scotland and Hungary, possibly also the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula" title="Iberian Peninsula" id="mwBow">Iberian Peninsula</a>, and where protected natural areas are close to human-dominated landscapes, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kruger_National_Park" title="Kruger National Park" id="mwBo0">Kruger National Park</a> in South Africa.<sup about="#mwt779" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Kruger_207-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Kruger"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Kruger-207"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Kruger-207" id="mwBo4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBo8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpA">[</span>206<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpE">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt782" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Oliveira_53-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Oliveira"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Oliveira-53"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Oliveira-53" id="mwBpI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBpM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpQ">[</span>52<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpU">]</span></span></a></sup> However, its introduction to places where no native felines are present also contributes to the decline of native species.<sup about="#mwt783" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-contr-ext_208-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"contr-ext"}}"><a href="#cite_note-contr-ext-208" id="mwBpY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBpc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpg">[</span>207<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="34" id="mwBpo" aria-labelledby="Ferality"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Ferality">Ferality</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt784" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBps" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Main","href":"./Template:Main"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Feral cat"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441" about="#mwt785" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt784" id="mwBpw">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feral_cat" title="Feral cat">Feral cat</a></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBp0"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Feral_cat_Virginia_crop.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBp4"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Feral_cat_Virginia_crop.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Feral_cat_Virginia_crop.jpg/250px-Feral_cat_Virginia_crop.jpg" decoding="async" data-file-width="1436" data-file-height="1672" data-file-type="bitmap" height="221" width="190" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Feral_cat_Virginia_crop.jpg/500px-Feral_cat_Virginia_crop.jpg 2x" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 0.75" id="mwBp8"></a><figcaption id="mwBqA">Feral <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farm_cat" title="Farm cat" id="mwBqE">farm cat</a></figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwBqI">Feral cats are domestic cats that were born in or have reverted to a wild state. They are unfamiliar with and wary of humans and roam freely in urban and rural areas.<sup about="#mwt788" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Rochlitz_209-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Rochlitz"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Rochlitz-209"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Rochlitz-209" id="mwBqM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBqQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqU">[</span>208<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqY">]</span></span></a></sup> The numbers of feral cats are not known, but estimates of the United States feral population range from 25 to 60 million.<sup about="#mwt789" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Rochlitz_209-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Rochlitz"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Rochlitz-209" id="mwBqc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBqg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqk">[</span>208<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqo">]</span></span></a></sup> Feral cats may live alone, but most are in large <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feral_cat_colonies" title="Feral cat colonies" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBqs">colonies</a>, which occupy a specific territory and are usually associated with a source of food.<sup about="#mwt792" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-hsus-feral_210-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"hsus-feral"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-hsus-feral-210"}}"><a href="#cite_note-hsus-feral-210" id="mwBqw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBq0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBq4">[</span>209<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBq8">]</span></span></a></sup> Famous feral cat colonies are in Rome around the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colosseum" title="Colosseum" id="mwBrA">Colosseum</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forum_Romanum" title="Forum Romanum" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBrE">Forum Romanum</a>, some being fed and given medical attention by volunteers.<sup about="#mwt795" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-211" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-211"}}"><a href="#cite_note-211" id="mwBrI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBrM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrQ">[</span>210<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBrY">Public attitudes toward feral cats vary widely, from seeing them as free-ranging pets to regarding them as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermin" title="Vermin" id="mwBrc">vermin</a>.<sup about="#mwt798" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-212" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-212"}}"><a href="#cite_note-212" id="mwBrg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBrk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBro">[</span>211<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="35" id="mwBrw" aria-labelledby="Impact_on_wildlife"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Impact_on_wildlife">Impact on wildlife</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt799" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBr0" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"main","href":"./Template:Main"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Cat predation on wildlife"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441" about="#mwt800" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt799" id="mwBr4">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_predation_on_wildlife" title="Cat predation on wildlife">Cat predation on wildlife</a></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBr8"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Feral_Cat_(5573630708).jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBsA"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Feral_Cat_(5573630708).jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Feral_Cat_%285573630708%29.jpg/250px-Feral_Cat_%285573630708%29.jpg" decoding="async" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="866" data-file-type="bitmap" height="211" width="250" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Feral_Cat_%285573630708%29.jpg/500px-Feral_Cat_%285573630708%29.jpg 2x" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBsE"></a><figcaption id="mwBsI">Cats kill billions of wild birds each year. This feral cat near <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane" title="Brisbane" id="mwBsM">Brisbane</a> has caught a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pale-headed_rosella" title="Pale-headed rosella" id="mwBsQ">Pale-headed rosella</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwBsU">Domestic cats are a contributing factor to the decline of several species, a factor that has ultimately led, in some cases, to extinction. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turnagra_capensis" title="Turnagra capensis" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBsY">The South Island piopio</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rallus_modestus" title="Rallus modestus" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBsc">Chatham rail</a>,<sup about="#mwt801" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Mead_1982_183–186_155-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Mead 1982 183–186"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Mead_1982_183–186-155" id="mwBsg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBsk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBso">[</span>154<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBss">]</span></span></a></sup> and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_merganser" title="New Zealand merganser" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBsw">New Zealand merganser</a><sup about="#mwt804" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-213" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-213"}}"><a href="#cite_note-213" id="mwBs0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBs4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBs8">[</span>212<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtA">]</span></span></a></sup> are a few from a long list, with the most extreme case being the flightless <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyall's_wren" title="Lyall's wren" id="mwBtE">Lyall's wren</a>, which was driven to extinction only a few years after its discovery.<sup about="#mwt808" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-214" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-214"}}"><a href="#cite_note-214" id="mwBtI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBtM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtQ">[</span>213<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt811" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-215" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-215"}}"><a href="#cite_note-215" id="mwBtY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBtc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtg">[</span>214<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtk">]</span></span></a></sup> One feral cat in New Zealand killed 102 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_lesser_short-tailed_bat" title="New Zealand lesser short-tailed bat" id="mwBto">New Zealand lesser short-tailed bats</a> in seven days.<sup about="#mwt814" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-216" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-216"}}"><a href="#cite_note-216" id="mwBts"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBtw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBt0">[</span>215<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBt4">]</span></span></a></sup> In the United States, feral and free-ranging domestic cats kill an estimated 6.3–22.3<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBt8"> </span>billion mammals annually.<sup about="#mwt815" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-NC012913_153-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"NC012913"}}"><a href="#cite_note-NC012913-153" id="mwBuA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBuE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuI">[</span>152<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBuQ">In Australia, one study found feral cats to kill 466 million reptiles per year. More than 258 reptile species were identified as being predated by cats.<sup about="#mwt818" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-217" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-217"}}"><a href="#cite_note-217" id="mwBuU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBuY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuc">[</span>216<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBug">]</span></span></a></sup> Cats have contributed to the extinction of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navassa_curly-tailed_lizard" title="Navassa curly-tailed lizard" id="mwBuk">Navassa curly-tailed lizard</a> and <i id="mwBuo"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chioninia_coctei" title="Chioninia coctei" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBus">Chioninia coctei</a>.</i><sup about="#mwt821" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-contr-ext_208-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"contr-ext"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-contr-ext-208"}}"><a href="#cite_note-contr-ext-208" id="mwBuw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBu0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBu4">[</span>207<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBu8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB14"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB18">[</span>236<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2A">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt889" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-238" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-238"}}"><a href="#cite_note-238" id="mwB2E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB2Y"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2c">[</span>238<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2g">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Chandoha" title="Walter Chandoha" id="mwB2k">Walter Chandoha</a> made his career photographing cats after his 1949 images of <i id="mwB2o">Loco</i>, a stray cat, were published. He is reported to have photographed 90,000 cats during his career and maintained an archive of 225,000 images that he drew from for publications during his lifetime.<sup about="#mwt895" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-240" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-240"}}"><a href="#cite_note-240" id="mwB2s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB2w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB20">[</span>239<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB24">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB28"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet_humanization" title="Pet humanization" id="mwB3A">Pet humanization</a> is a form of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropomorphism" title="Anthropomorphism" id="mwB3E">anthropomorphism</a> in which cats are kept for companionship and treated more like human family members than traditional pets.<sup about="#mwt898" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-241" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-241"}}"><a href="#cite_note-241" id="mwB3I"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3M"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3Q">[</span>240<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3U">]</span></span></a></sup> This trend of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet_culture" title="Pet culture" id="mwB3Y">pet culture</a> involves providing cats with a higher level of care, attention and often even luxury, similar to the way humans are treated.<sup about="#mwt901" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-242" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-242"}}"><a href="#cite_note-242" id="mwB3c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3k">[</span>241<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3o">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="37" id="mwB3s" aria-labelledby="Shows"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Shows">Shows</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt902" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB3w" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"main","href":"./Template:Main"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Cat show"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441" about="#mwt903" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt902" id="mwB30">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_show" title="Cat show">Cat show</a></div>

<p id="mwB34">A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_show" title="Cat show" id="mwB38">cat show</a> is a judged event in which the owners of cats compete to win titles in various cat-registering organizations by entering their cats to be judged after a breed standard.<sup about="#mwt906" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-How_Stuff_Works-2008_243-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"How Stuff Works-2008"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-How_Stuff_Works-2008-243"}}"><a href="#cite_note-How_Stuff_Works-2008-243" id="mwB4A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB4E"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4I">[</span>242<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4M">]</span></span></a></sup> It is often required that a cat must be healthy and vaccinated to participate in a cat show.<sup about="#mwt907" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-How_Stuff_Works-2008_243-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"How Stuff Works-2008"}}"><a href="#cite_note-How_Stuff_Works-2008-243" id="mwB4Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB4U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4Y">[</span>242<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4c">]</span></span></a></sup> Both <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedigree_(cat)" title="Pedigree (cat)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB4g">pedigreed</a> and non-<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purebred" title="Purebred" id="mwB4k">purebred</a> companion ("moggy") cats are admissible, although the rules differ depending on the organization. Competing cats are compared to the applicable breed standard, and assessed for temperament.<sup about="#mwt908" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-How_Stuff_Works-2008_243-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"How Stuff Works-2008"}}"><a href="#cite_note-How_Stuff_Works-2008-243" id="mwB4o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB4s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4w">[</span>242<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB40">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="38" id="mwB44" aria-labelledby="Infection"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Infection">Infection</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt909" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB48" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Main","href":"./Template:Main"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Feline zoonosis"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441" about="#mwt910" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt909" id="mwB5A">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feline_zoonosis" title="Feline zoonosis">Feline zoonosis</a></div>

<p id="mwB5E">Cats can be infected or infested with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus" title="Virus" id="mwB5I">viruses</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogenic_bacteria" title="Pathogenic bacteria" id="mwB5M">pathogenic bacteria</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus" title="Fungus" id="mwB5Q">fungus</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protozoans" title="Protozoans" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB5U">protozoans</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod" title="Arthropod" id="mwB5Y">arthropods</a> or worms that can transmit diseases to humans; infections of most concern include <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salmonella" title="Salmonella" id="mwB5c">salmonella</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat-scratch_disease" title="Cat-scratch disease" id="mwB5g">cat-scratch disease</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxoplasmosis" title="Toxoplasmosis" id="mwB5k">toxoplasmosis</a>.<sup about="#mwt913" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Chomel2014_244-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Chomel2014"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Chomel2014-244"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Chomel2014-244" id="mwB5o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB5s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5w">[</span>243<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB50">]</span></span></a></sup> In some cases, the cat exhibits no <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symptoms" title="Symptoms" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB54">symptoms</a> of the disease.<sup about="#mwt916" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Ohio2016_245-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Ohio2016"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Ohio2016-245"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Ohio2016-245" id="mwB58"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB6A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6E">[</span>244<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6I">]</span></span></a></sup> The same disease can then become evident in a human.<sup about="#mwt919" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Goldstein2015_246-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Goldstein2015"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Goldstein2015-246"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Goldstein2015-246" id="mwB6M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB6Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6U">[</span>245<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6Y">]</span></span></a></sup> The likelihood that a person will become diseased depends on the age and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immunocompetence" title="Immunocompetence" id="mwB6c">immune status</a> of the person. Others might also acquire infections from cat <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feces" title="Feces" id="mwB6g">feces</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasite" title="Parasite" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB6k">parasites</a> exiting the cat's body.<sup about="#mwt920" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Chomel2014_244-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Chomel2014"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Chomel2014-244" id="mwB6o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB6s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6w">[</span>243<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB60">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt923" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-StullBrophy2015_247-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"StullBrophy2015"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-StullBrophy2015-247"}}"><a href="#cite_note-StullBrophy2015-247" id="mwB64"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB68"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7A">[</span>246<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7E">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
